issues.description: The master contains a directory placeholder and the README expects a consistent 00 Code/01 Raw Data/02 Intermediate Data/03 Final Data/04 Output project layout.

The datasheet calls CBI, CIR and CIR-request data proprietary and not publicly distributable. Official BELab products provide controlled-access candidates with anonymized identifiers and reported periods that do not by themselves establish source-field/key compatibility or this user’s authorization. Exact current access is unknown, not proven unavailable.

Author documentation describes CBI fiscal years 2012–2020, while file 20 reads 2009_2022.dta and applies any>=2010 for lag/lead construction. Confirm the intended native file, effective period, fields and join keys; the two period descriptions are not interchangeable.

The datasheet describes CIR December extracts for 2013–2020, but file 11 reads SOC December files from 2000–2015 for relationship construction and 14-year lags. The additional 2000–2012 history, including 2000–2009, is a real source dependency; verify its native schema and continuity with the later CIR files.

Four independently consumed bank/firm province maps are referenced by exact files/keys, while the datasheet only says bank headquarters provinces were manually identified. Their exact source, construction, value definitions and historical coverage are not supplied.

File 12 reads `$FIN/identifiers_region_industry.dta` but no supplied source writes that exact table. The HHI consumer proves only the CIF join and province field used; the exact table producer/mapping remains unestablished.

File 10 saves end_of_year_credit_2013_2020.dta under FIN and file 20 also consumes it under FIN; file 60 line 1421 instead reads the same product under RAW. A one-line working-copy repair is source-supported.

File 60 builds the 2016–2019 BIG/MEDIUM object from Block1, applies its visible firm/legal-form/industry/credit filters, complete-case and singleton drops, trims and winsorization, and creates `detailed` plus both exposure/assets outcomes through line 1496. Table 11 immediately uses this in-memory object; the later explicit large/medium RD-plot section reloads `$FIN\final_database_firml_BIG.dta` and recreates `opt_h`. No save connects those source locations. Inference from the matching population label, source order, and downstream fields: the just-built object appears intended for the later reload. A separate save after line 1496 and before the first `gen opt_h` is a conditional persistence repair; row/ID/field/population equivalence remains future validation.

Raw data were obtained from three different con�idential databases provided by Banco de

The second database is the Central Credit Registry of Spain or Central de Información de Riesgos
(CIR), which is maintained by the Banco de Españ a in its capacity as the primary banking

of outstanding loans issued to non�inancial �irms by all banks operating in Spain. The primary
raw data consists of monthly extracts provided by employees of the Banco de Españ a in 2021. I
use the December extracts from each year from 2013 to 2020 to ensure that the data from CBI
and CIR are measured at the same point in time, as over 99% of �irms have their �iscal year
ending in December. Note that CIR variables are forwarded in my analysis, so my sample period
ends in 2019. I drop loan-year observations from non-depository institutions or with negative
or zero outstanding credit amounts. From these extracts, I build a loan-level panel that includes

evidence.quote:
�irm and bank identi�iers, the outstanding credit amount, and loan types. I complement this
panel by downloading and merging information on interest rates, which is only available from
2018, and by manually identifying the province where the headquarters of each bank are
located. This panel allows me to construct the majority of the aggregated �irm-level variables

evidence.description: Datasheet describes CIR information requests for potential borrowers and interprets them as loan applications.
evidence.quote:
The third source of data employed in the paper includes all banks’ requests for information from
the CIR on potential borrowers. By law, a bank may only request CIR information on potential
borrowers when the borrower “seriously approaches the bank to obtain credit” (i.e., applies for
a loan). Because banks receive monthly updates on the credit exposures and loan defaults of

their current borrowers, further requests for CIR information are only useful if the �irm is not
already a borrower. Therefore, I interpret banks’ requests for information as loan applications
from potential borrowers.
